description: Game-side values of AdaptOrDeity: the environment (food packets), the colony and the ranges of the player's controls, each with its source. Physiological parameters of the cells are not here: they live upstream in circulatory-autogen-modules modules/cell/generic_adaptive_cell/parameters.json and reach the game inside the assembled kernel (its parameters), so the game reads them from the kernel. Values are canonical SI. status: sourced, placeholder (needs a source), design (a game choice), definitional.

food.packet_trace_minor_share.note: other trace species relative to the main one

food.dry_mass_fraction.note: share of a cell's mass that is not water: E. coli dry weight ~2.8e-13 g of ~9.5e-13 g wet (~30%; 70% water, BioNumbers). A food packet is a dead cell or organic particle of the same make-up (confidence medium: aggregates and mucilage hold more water)

food.dry_carbon_fraction.note: carbon's share of a bacterium's dry mass: ~50% (Neidhardt 1990; BioNumbers). With body.cell_density (1.1 g/mL) and food.dry_mass_fraction (0.3) a packet holds 1100 x 0.3 x 0.5 / 0.012011 = 13,700 mol C/m3, i.e. 2,290 mol glucose equivalents/m3 (2.3 M; 6 C per glucose). Medium confidence: the game counts all of a dead cell's carbon as glucose equivalents, though protein and nucleic acid would need other enzymes

food.carbon_molar_mass.note: molar mass of carbon (IUPAC standard atomic weight 12.011)

food.carbons_per_glucose.note: carbon atoms in a glucose (C6H12O6): a packet's carbon counted in glucose equivalents

food.free_fraction.note: share of a packet's glucose equivalents already small molecules: a bacterium's pool of free metabolites is ~3-4% of its dry mass (E. coli), taken as the same share of its carbon. At the packet density (2.3 M glucose equivalents) that is ~70 mM of free sugar inside the particle, consistent with food.contact_glucose (50 mM at a touching membrane). To check

food.free_leak_rate.note: rate the free small molecules leak out of a packet (a lysed cell): first order, ~10 min time constant; no source yet

food.contact_glucose.note: free sugar in a packet (or a vacuole) at which enzymes stop cutting its polymer (product inhibition), so the most the membrane facing it sees: a fresh packet holds ~70 mM of free sugar (food.free_fraction of 2.3 M), and hydrolysis tops it up only below this level. A touching cell sees the packet's free sugar on the share of its membrane facing it (the cap the packet covers, ~5% for a fresh packet) and the environment field on the rest (2026-10-13; it was the whole membrane's glucose under the retired contact rule)

food.contact_trace.note: a packet's main trace species per its free sugar, as concentrations (per food.contact_glucose): it releases contact_trace / contact_glucose (2e-4) mol of its main trace with each mol of glucose that leaks into the water

food.packet_radius.note: radius of a fresh packet: 0.5 um, smaller than the cell, so it holds about a quarter of a 0.8 um packet's food at the same density and runs out sooner (designer, 2026-10-14: smaller packets that run out faster); it shrinks as it is eaten

food.carrier_speed.note: speed of a creature carrying food (prey, or an ally bringing it) over the ground: 1 um/s, slower than a swimming bacterium (~20 um/s) so it can be met

food.lying_density.note: food lying on the ground per area when the field is first filled: about 32 packets in the 30 um view (32 / (30 um)^2), 8x the earlier 4 as packets hold ~8x less (2026-10-12). Later lying food comes with the arrivals

food.used_up_fraction.note: a packet with less than this share of its glucose left is used up and removed

food.entry_angle_spread.note: carried packets enter heading inwards within half this angle either side of the normal

food.field_half_size.note: half the side of the square field around the colony

food.initial_packet_capacity.note: packets the first snapshot frames have room for; frames grow when more are in the field

food.seed.note: random seed of the food field (determinism)

colony.cell_gap.note: gap between neighbouring cells of a colony (centres 2 R_cell + gap apart)

controls.growth_max.note: most ATP a cell may put into growth, in multiples of its resting turnover: growing fermenters run glycolysis 10-40x their maintenance flux; the cell can reach ~40x on food

controls.expression_min.note: lowest expression a player can choose (two octaves below the calibrated cell; user decision 2026-10-08)

controls.expression_max.note: highest expression a player can choose (two octaves above)

environment.current_speed.note: amplitude of the tidal current over the ground above the seabed's boundary layer: 0.2 um/s, slower than the creature swims (1.3 um/s per flagellum), so swimming beats the drift (designer, 2026-10-14); it flows along the heading and back with the tide

environment.tide_period.note: period of the tidal current: the principal lunar semidiurnal tide M2, 12.42 h; the current is amplitude x cos(2 pi t / period), so it slows, turns and flows back twice a day

motility.mean_run.note: mean length of a run with the motor on (random, exponential; E. coli runs ~1 s between tumbles)

motility.mean_pause.note: mean pause with the motor off between runs (random, exponential); each run sets off in a random direction

motility.seed.note: random seed of the runs and pauses (determinism)

body.cell_density.note: cell density about 1.1 g/mL (BioNumbers): the mass of the body for its momentum, and W/kg for display

motility.thrust_angle_sd.note: standard deviation of each flagellum's thrust direction about straight away from its base: 10 degrees, normal, drawn per run (user decision 2026-10-09); it turns the body, so runs curve

motility.thrust_scale.note: flagellar thrust as a share of the cell model's (v_one, a single flagellum's free-swimming speed, 15 um/s as for E. coli): 0.1, so the creature moves 10x slower (designer, 2026-10-14: the creature moved too fast); a game-side design choice, the physiology upstream keeps its sourced value

motility.proton_cost_scale.note: protons per flagellar revolution as a share of the cell model's (n_H_rev): the thrust scale squared, since the mechanical power of a scaled thrust (force x speed) scales with its square, so swimming keeps a bacterium's ~0.1-2% efficiency (designer, 2026-10-14: bring the flagella cost down with the thrust; stronger flagella proteins later raise both)

motility.flagellum_spacing.note: where new flagella are placed by default: around the back of the cell, this far apart

scoring.survival_points.note: skill points the survival meter converts to at 100/100 when a level ends (designer request 2026-10-13: no food points; survival and reproduction points). In proportion below, rounded. Calibrated 2026-10-14 with the scripted players (docs/plans/scoring.md): with damage 5 at full, a perfect level 1 earns 15 (three stars)

scoring.damage_points.note: skill points the damage meter converts to at 100/100 when a level ends; in proportion below, rounded. The damage meter is 100 x (1 - the worst mean damage load of the creature in the level), a dead cell counting as a lethal load

scoring.starving_atp_fraction.note: a living cell is starving while its ATP is below this fraction of its resting level; the survival meter falls in proportion to the share of the creature's living cells starving (all of it once none lives). 0.4 (was 0.5, 2026-10-15): a cell regulating its maintenance by ATP holds about 4 mM through a gap between meals, and holding it is coping, not starving (docs/plans/scoring.md)

scoring.starvation_to_empty.note: the survival meter empties after this share of the level's survival time spent with every cell starving (0.6 of a day at level 1); it falls in proportion to the share of cells starving

scoring.damage_to_empty.note: the damage meter empties when the level has added this much damage, as a share of a lethal load (mean over the creature's cells, a dead one counting as a full load). 0.5 (was 0.1, 2026-10-15): cutting maintenance through famines now costs envelope and ribosome damage, about a fifth of a lethal load in level 1 for a player who regulates it by ATP (docs/plans/scoring.md)

scoring.star_points_1.note: points a level must earn (its meters and its reproduction points) for star 1: 5 / 12 / 14 match the scripted players at level 1 (left alone dies, mediocre 11, great 13, optimised 15; docs/plans/scoring.md, 2026-10-15)

scoring.star_points_2.note: points a level must earn (its meters and its reproduction points) for star 2: 5 / 12 / 14 match the scripted players at level 1 (left alone dies, mediocre 11, great 13, optimised 15; docs/plans/scoring.md, 2026-10-15)

scoring.star_points_3.note: points a level must earn (its meters and its reproduction points) for star 3: 5 / 12 / 14 match the scripted players at level 1 (left alone dies, mediocre 11, great 13, optimised 15; docs/plans/scoring.md, 2026-10-15)

skills.points_per_offspring.note: reproduction points: skill points per daughter released in the creature's lineage (its own daughters at division without multicellularity, and its free organisms' daughters, any generation: designer request 2026-10-13), on top of the food points (designer request 2026-10-12: offspring are fitness, so staying single-celled pays for a while). Measured 2026-10-12 (one seed): a level-2 cell kept on food (0.01 packets/s) at growth 3 left 5 daughters in the week (74 food points); at the level's own food (3e-3 packets/s) growth 2-10 runs its ATP out within a day and it leaves none. Set to 1 point per daughter (designer, 2026-10-12)

field.fine_spacing.note: cell side of the finest grid, around the colony (designer decision 2026-10-12)

field.fine_margin.note: water the finest grid covers beyond the colony on each side: room for the grids to recentre by whole coarse cells (4 um) and for the coarse flux at the fine grid's edge to be away from the cells

field.fine_substeps.note: steps the finest grid takes per macro step for glucose (the coarser grids, and lactate, acid and the smells, take one): Douglas steps damp short modes slowly, so a moving cell's own near field lags. A sink drifting at 2 um/s (the current) sees its membrane depletion 7% short with 1, 0.7% with 4, +0.1% with 8; swimming at 20 um/s 16%, 4% and 1% short (NestedFieldTests, 2026-10-13). Lactate and acid at the membrane barely act back on the cell, so they take one

field.trace_stride.note: the smells (trace species) take one field step every this many macro steps (1 s), with what packets released meanwhile: nothing reads them every step (they are for sensing at level 3), and they were 4 of the 7 species the field steps (one cell: 156 -> ~80 us a step, 2026-10-13). Content is exact; Douglas steps keep the steady state

field.extent_multiple.note: the outermost grid spans at least this multiple of the colony's diameter (designer decision 2026-10-12); grids have 4x the spacing and extent of the next finer one

field.layer_depth.note: depth of the 2D water layer the field holds: about the distance diffusion mixes in one 0.1 s exchange (sqrt(2 D dt) = 12 um for glucose); the water above it is not represented yet (a 3D correction would add it)

field.diffusivity.glucose.note: glucose in water, 6.73e-10 m2/s at 25 C (about 10% lower at 20 C)

field.diffusivity.lactate.note: lactate anion in water: ~1.0e-9 m2/s, typical of small organic anions; needs a measured value

field.diffusivity.acid.note: the field carries acid as buffered H+ equivalents, moved by the mobile carbonate buffer: bicarbonate's diffusivity at 20 C (1.18e-9 at 25 C). Free H+ (9.3e-9) is ~1e-4 of the acid at pH 7.3, so its own diffusion is negligible

field.diffusivity.oxygen.note: O2 in water at ~20-25 C (2.0e-9 at 20 C, 2.4e-9 at 25 C in Han & Bartels; 2.1e-9 used)

field.diffusivity.aspartate.note: amino acids of aspartate's size diffuse at ~0.8-0.9e-9 m2/s at 25 C (glycine 1.06e-9, alanine 0.91e-9); aspartate's own value to check

field.diffusivity.serine.note: near alanine's 0.91e-9 m2/s at 25 C; serine's own value to check

field.diffusivity.ribose.note: a pentose, a little faster than glucose (6.73e-10 at 25 C); to check

field.diffusivity.dimethylsulfide.note: dimethyl sulfide in water at ~20 C; value to check against the paper

environment.oxygen.note: O2 in the surface ocean at ~0.1% of present atmospheric O2 (mid-Proterozoic estimate); 0.25 mol/m3 today at 20 C. Nothing takes it up yet

environment.carbonate_total.note: dissolved inorganic carbon of the 2 Ga ocean: ~10 PAL CO2 (paleosols ~2.2 Ga) gives ~0.15 mM CO2 and ~3 mM HCO3- at pH 7.3. Sets the buffer that turns acid into pH

environment.carbonate_pk1.note: first carbonic acid dissociation constant (pK1*) in seawater at ~20 C, S 35; to check

field.input_tolerance.note: a cell's membrane concentrations from the field reach its module only when they moved by more than this share of their departure from the open water (the sea's glucose, no lactate, the sea's H+) since they last did: every changed input restarts the cell's integrator. Relative to the departure, a lone cell's own 0.07% depletion reaches it (to 1% of that); the earlier rule, relative to the value, hid it (2026-10-13). colony-bench 512 cells, 20 s, 1 thread: 1.06 s before (old rule), 1.22 s now with field.fine_substeps; the reference passes every change. The exchange stays exact (it uses the cell's own fluxes)

field.reference_substeps.note: field steps per macro step in the reference environment (FieldAccuracy.Reference): lambda = D dt / dx^2 about 1.6 for the acid at 1 um and 0.1/64 s; tests check the reference is converged in it

field.reference_cell_tolerance.note: cells relative tolerance in the reference environment

prey.radius.note: radius of a prey cell: half the creature's 1 um cell, so a cell can engulf it (marine bacteria are often 0.2-1 um across). Its content is a sphere of this radius at the packet density (1.2e-15 mol glucose equivalents), with the packet's free share

prey.run_speed.note: swimming speed of prey over the ground during a run: 3 um/s, slower than swimming bacteria (20-30 um/s) so the creature can meet them

prey.mean_run.note: mean run before a tumble (exponential); each tumble sets a new heading at random. E. coli runs ~1 s

prey.initial_capacity.note: prey the first snapshot frames have room for; frames grow when more are in view

organisms.max.note: most free-living organisms (released daughters and their offspring) simulated at once; a new daughter beyond it replaces a dead one, else freezes the one farthest from the creature (kept as it was: organisms.frozen_max). Measured cost: see docs/plans/free-daughters.md

organisms.frozen_max.note: most free organisms kept frozen out of range (designer request 2026-10-13: far organisms and bodies are remembered and frozen until the creature comes back). Each holds its cell (measured ~80 kB of memory with its integrator), so 256 take ~20 MB; beyond it the frozen organism farthest from the creature is forgotten (counted as gone)

organisms.frozen_bodies_max.note: most dead bodies kept frozen out of range (a few hundred bytes each); beyond it the frozen body farthest from the creature is forgotten (FoodField.BodiesGone)

organisms.range_view_widths.note: a free organism farther than this many view widths (2 x food.field_half_size) from the creature, along either ground axis, is no longer simulated (gone out of range); beyond the view it sees only the open water, with no food packets. A dead organism's body (food) stays within the same range, though other food stays within the view

organisms.initial_capacity.note: free organisms the first snapshot frames have room for; frames grow when there are more

seabed.ground_depth.note: height of the ground below where the creature starts (the world is a vertical slice of water, y upwards): 40 um, clear of the tallest structure (a stack of three 7 um rocks stands ~25 um) and of the 15 um food window, so the creature starts in open water and swims down to reach the seabed

seabed.boundary_layer.note: the current grows linearly from zero at the ground (no slip) to full speed at this height

seabed.stretch_width.note: each stretch of seabed this wide holds one structure (a boulder, a stack of rocks or an arch)

seabed.wake_length.note: length of the sheltered wake behind a rock, in rock radii (the current recovers linearly over it)

minimap.tile_size.note: side of a minimap tile: the map remembers, per tile the creature has had in view, the water it saw there (glucose, lactate, pH) and whether it is rock or ground; 5 um, a few cell widths, so the 30 um view covers 6 x 6 tiles

minimap.sample_interval.note: simulated time between updates of the minimap's memory from the creature's view

luck.max.note: the most luck points Luck can hold (adapting_plan.md, Luck)

luck.start.note: luck points at the start of a game

luck.rate.note: luck points gained per second of game time: empty to full in 3 h

luck.cost_rate.note: luck points a current costs per second at full strength (in proportion below): a full store blows for 100 s

luck.max_speed.note: flow of Luck's current on its axis at full strength: 2 um/s, faster than the creature swims (~1.5 um/s) and 10x the tide

luck.half_width.note: half the width of the band of water Luck's current flows along (a few cell radii)

luck.full_length.note: length of the aimed arrow that gives full strength (the view's width); shorter arrows blow in proportion

trace_species.name: Aspartate
trace_species.note: an E. coli Tar attractant (adapting_plan.md: smell at level 3)

trace_species.name: Ribose
trace_species.note: sensed through Trg and the ribose-binding protein

trace_species.name: Dimethyl sulfide
trace_species.note: a marine infochemical of algal origin

references.han1996oxygen: Han, P. and Bartels, D. M. (1996) Temperature dependence of oxygen diffusion in H2O and D2O. Journal of Physical Chemistry 100, 5597-5602
